description: Catch-all nil for a Patrick query that carries NO surname at all — the 'drop the surname, anchor on givenName plus jurisdiction' lever the skill reaches for late in nil exhaustion, to catch records whose surname was mis-transcribed or omitted by the indexer. Its sibling record-search-flynn-any-variant-no-results absorbs any Fl* SURNAME, but predicate matching requires every key in the predicate to be PRESENT in the args, so a query with no surname key misses it and came back a fixture_not_found ERROR (observed on ut_search_records_018, v1_2026-08-06_22-32-13, where Tool Arguments was scored 2 for it). This absorbs those. Keep it LAST in the test's mcp_fixtures list, after the surname-anchored catch-all — matching is first-match-wins in list order, and this predicate is the loosest of the set, so any earlier position would shadow the specific spellings and erase the expected_args signal Tool Arguments is graded on. Anchored to the given name on purpose: a query naming neither Patrick nor a Flynn surname is a genuinely wrong search and still misses.
